source_user: A service receives a mix of short prompts and long generations. Design an evaluation plan that reports TTFT, TPOT, throughput, queueing, and P99 latency. Scenario variant 112: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: separate prefill and decode behavior; fix workload distribution; report warmup; use repeated trials; capture GPU memory and request-level traces.
corrected_answer: Assume a fixed model, tokenizer, hardware, serving configuration, concurrency policy, and request mix; treat all rates as measured rather than inferred. Hypothesis for variant 112: under the prespecified mixed short-prompt/long-generation workload, continuous admission reduces median queue time and improves goodput versus the baseline without increasing P99 end-to-end latency by more than 10%. Run a randomized paired A/B experiment with identical seeded requests, warm up and discard a declared number of requests, then repeat enough independent trials to report confidence intervals and stop only at a prespecified precision or safety limit. Record arrival, queue, dispatch, prefill start/end, first-token, each decode step, completion, error, and cancellation timestamps. Report TTFT (arrival to first token, with queue-inclusive and service-only variants), TPOT (decode time divided by generated-token count, excluding or including the first-token interval explicitly), queue-time distribution, throughput and goodput denominators, and P99 latency, stratified by prompt and output-length bins. Separate prefill from decode utilization, and collect GPU memory, KV-cache occupancy, compute/utilization, power/thermal state, CPU, and OOM/timeout/correctness telemetry. Confounders include cache state, arrival burstiness, length mix, batching policy, throttling, and thermal drift. Roll back if correctness changes, OOM/eviction or timeout rates rise, or P99 exceeds the agreed guardrail; do not generalize beyond the tested workload and hardware without new evidence.
risks: Queue-inclusive and service-only latency can be conflated.
A changed request mix or cache state can make the A/B comparison invalid.
P99 and goodput are unstable if denominators and trial count are not prespecified.
evidence_required: Versioned workload/configuration manifest, randomized pairing record, request-level timestamps, length strata, GPU/KV/CPU/thermal telemetry, correctness and failure logs, and repeated-trial uncertainty estimates.
